clue.text: Seductive dancer Sal has nothing for me

parts.note: nothing is zero, the round letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl called Sal refuses to give the speaker anything.
explanation.walkthrough: SALOME danced the dance of the seven veils for Herod in the Bible story.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical princess is famed for the seductive veil dance before Herod.

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether financial profits are being paid to a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital gains' reads as a tax phrase, but 'Capital' alone is the definition and 'doctor' is a verb signalling the anagram of GAINS TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the seat of government of Chile.

parts.note: a local is the British word for a neighbourhood pub, so its manager is the person licensed to sell drink there

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a nearby business.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's nearest pub; its landlord holds the licence to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord holds the licence to serve alcohol, hence the title.

definitions.meaning: to encounter is to come across someone
a gathering of riders and hounds for a fox hunt

explanation.definitionFit: To come face to face with someone; also a hunting assembly of riders and hounds.

clue.text: Scanning the books for money owing on the horses

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' places the money owing after the horses

parts.note: a stud is a stable of horses kept for breeding
IOUs are written promises of money owed

explanation.surface: Poring over the accounts to find debts run up by betting.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bookmaker checking ledgers, but the definition is someone reading books diligently.
explanation.definitionFit: A diligent reader spends time poring over books, so is bookish.

clue.text: It certainly was a crucial moment for Lot's wife

definitions.text: It certainly was a crucial moment for Lot's wife

parts.words: It certainly was a crucial moment for Lot's wife
parts.note: in Genesis Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and was changed into a pillar of salt, a decisive moment that also literally altered her

explanation.surface: A remark about a decisive moment in the Bible story of Lot's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a decisive moment is read literally: she was turned into a pillar, a point of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive moment of change; Lot's wife was transformed into a salt pillar.

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh man's name, short for David

explanation.surface: A man from Wales is taking up a position.
explanation.walkthrough: DAI is the crossword's typical Welshman; his possessive 's gives the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker is a stand.

clue.text: Small number elevated to job connected with computers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it upwards

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
a line is a line of work, a job

explanation.surface: A minor figure gets promoted to a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns NO upwards to ON in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being connected to a network of computers is being on the internet.

clue.text: Is in a hide to see a bird

indicators.note: the word in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sits concealed in a hide to watch a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' suggests the birdwatcher's shelter, but it is an animal skin, into which IS goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

definitions.meaning: scored here means cut with a mark or notch
caught as a criminal is arrested, or in British slang stolen

explanation.definitionFit: Notched with a small cut; also British slang for arrested by the police.

parts.note: pieces of writing for newspapers; the word for them also means items or things in general

explanation.surface: A plain description of written pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Items or objects, and also written pieces for a newspaper or magazine.

parts.note: a little devil is a rascal
may expresses permission, as can does
to care is to show concern

explanation.surface: A rash rogue proves capable of worrying after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts recklessness with concern; the three pieces join into the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless and carefree, careless of consequences.

parts.note: pub staff work in public houses, but bar men can also be barristers, who work in the London legal societies of that name

explanation.surface: Asks where different bar staff are employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Barristers are members of the Bar and belong to the four legal Inns of Court in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs or hotels employ bar staff; barristers belong to the Inns of Court.

clue.text: With revision tries to take the examination again

indicators.note: revising the word tries means altering its letters

explanation.surface: A student revises hard and has another go at the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' suggests study before an exam, but it signals the anagram of TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A second attempt at a failed exam.

indicators.note: in an across clue, 'on' places the turned piece after the other
turns here means the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: Something rounds on whoever opposes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It turns on' reads as a thing rounding on someone; 'turns' is the reversal and 'on' sets it after AN in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone against a cause is an opponent of it.

indicators.note: topless removes the top letter of the word in this down clue

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: A promiscuous relation is spotted without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot is to unfasten it.

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of forth are arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Something pours out bubbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forth' suggests motion but is anagram fodder signalled by 'somehow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foam is a mass of small bubbles.

clue.text: Colourful digits useful in the nursery

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: the gift a good gardener has in a plant nursery

parts.note: green is a colour
fingers are digits

explanation.surface: Painted fingers come in handy in a children's room.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is a plant nursery, not a child's room; green fingers is the British phrase for gardening skill (green thumb in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: A talent for growing plants is valuable to a gardener or plant grower.

definitions.meaning: the novelist William ... Maugham's first name in practice
a large neoclassical building on the Strand in London

explanation.definitionFit: The novelist was known as W. Somerset Maugham; Somerset House is a London landmark.

definitions.meaning: read as in-come, those who have come in or been let in

explanation.definitionFit: Allowed entry; and 'income' read as having come in, i.e. let in.

clue.text: Company with some of the stocks sought by mountaineers

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for what climbers look for

parts.note: a firm is a company
the old stocks held offenders by the feet, so each hole was a foothold

explanation.surface: A business with a share portfolio attracts climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' suggests shares, but it is the wooden punishment frame that held feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers need a secure place for their feet on rock.

clue.text: Ascent is difficult for the poor

parts.note: hard means difficult
up is the direction of an ascent

explanation.surface: Climbing is tough for those without money.
explanation.definitionFit: Short of money is the idiomatic sense.

indicators.note: oral indicates something spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: pleas are entreaties

explanation.surface: Spoken requests win approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To give satisfaction is to win approval.

parts.note: a political turning point read literally as the rod on which a wheel spins

explanation.surface: A decisive moment during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests politics, but here a wheel revolves about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel rotates around this central rod.
Lying flat, and the habit of telling untruths.

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: peril is danger

explanation.surface: Unending menace awaits a sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a fairy-like being.

clue.text: A letter less than perfect in conception

indicators.note: one letter fewer than the word for perfect, losing its final letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A single letter makes something imperfect from its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or thought is a conception.

clue.text: Take forty winks-or less than twelve

indicators.note: less than means the word for twelve falls short by a letter

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: A nap, or a number under twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than twelve' is DOZEN short of its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is a short sleep, a light nap.

clue.text: It's twice as expensive. What a pity!

indicators.note: twice means the word is given two times

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: Something costs double, which is a shame.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of dismay or sympathy.

clue.text: Make much of Tesco's new blend

indicators.note: a new blend mixes the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: the supermarket name with its S

explanation.surface: Praise for a supermarket's latest coffee or tea blend.
explanation.walkthrough: TESCO is a British supermarket chain; its letters with the S are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to make much of someone.

indicators.note: including places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the press is the newspapers
ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: Newspapers carry long-term weather outlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long-range' looks part of the forecasts but gives AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens or predictions of what is to come.

clue.text: Took a breather in Desert Storm'

indicators.note: to storm is to rage, so the letters of desert are thrown about

explanation.surface: Soldiers paused during the Gulf War operation Desert Storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Storm was the 1991 Gulf War operation; 'Storm' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Took a breather means paused to recover.
